findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permissions, truncated read)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path causes thread panic instead of returning a typed domain error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, use map_err on fs::read_to_string to convert io::Error into a domain error type, and propagate with ?

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric input for the value field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (non-numeric value) aborts the thread instead of yielding a typed parse error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, use ? on parse::<u32>() mapped to a ParseError variant, and remove unwrap entirely

findings.problem: lossy `as u16` cast on the result of parse::<u32>() silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a value of 70000 becomes 4448 without any error or warning, corrupting domain data
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(value) and propagate error via Result, or validate value <= u16::MAX before casting

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec<String> for every line when only two fields are needed; also uses unchecked indexing parts[0] and parts[1]
findings.failure_mode: out-of-bounds access on lines with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields causes panic; excessive allocation per line
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to extract the first delimiter pair, handle None for missing fields, avoid collect/Vec allocation, and access via the two returned options directly

findings.problem: println!() is a side effect embedded in data-loading logic inside the function body
findings.failure_mode: side effects in core logic make the function non-deterministic, untestable without capturing stdout, and violate the pure-core imperative-shell boundary
findings.fix: remove println! from the core; if logging is needed, let the shell layer handle it, or return a separate diagnostic type from the pure function

findings.problem: I/O (fs::read_to_string) is mixed into the same function as parsing and data construction, with no separation of pure calculations from imperative shell
findings.failure_mode: the function cannot be unit-tested without a real filesystem, cannot be composed with other data sources, and couples domain logic to filesystem access
findings.fix: split into two functions: a pure `fn parse_records(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>` for the core, and an imperative shell `fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>` that reads the file and delegates to the pure function

findings.problem: value is a raw u16 with no domain constraints (e.g., valid range, non-zero)
findings.failure_mode: illegal values (e.g., 0, overflowed values) are representable, making it impossible for the compiler to enforce domain invariants
findings.fix: use a newtype `pub struct Value(u16)` with a fallible constructor `Value::new(u16) -> Result<Value, ValueError>` that enforces domain constraints

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_sessions; the function allocates a Vec<String> per line and collects into Vec<Record>
findings.failure_mode: allocation behavior is unmeasured; for large files this creates O(n) intermediate allocations that could be eliminated with a pre-allocated Vec and split_once
findings.fix: add a criterion or divan benchmark measuring allocations via `test::black_box`, then optimize to pre-allocate Vec<Record> with try_reserve and use split_once to avoid per-line Vec<String>

findings.problem: No dev-dependencies for testing (e.g., proptest, tempfile) and no benchmark configuration in Cargo.toml
findings.failure_mode: behavior tests, property tests, and allocation benchmarks cannot be run from the crate
findings.fix: add proptest and tempfile to dev-dependencies for property-based and integration testing; add [[bench]] section if benchmarks are planned

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions allocation or throughput behavior
no profiler data (flamegraph, perf) to validate allocation patterns
no allocation tracking (e.g., criterion's measurement, alloc_counter) evidence
no second-ring evidence such as Kani proofs, Miri UB checks, or property tests
no CLI/command-line integration test exercising the full load_sessions workflow
residual_risk: static review only with no commands run; all five forbidden constructs (unwrap, as-cast, println! side-effect, unchecked indexing via split+collect, no error propagation) are present and would cause panics or data corruption under malformed input; the crate as written does not meet Holzman Rust gates
